blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Chain-of-thought traces are widely read as records of how models reach their answers, informing debugging, agent auditing, and claims about reasoning. Testing this interpretation is difficult because natural-language thinking traces are rarely mechanically verifiable. We revisit it in iGSM, a synthetic grade-school mathematics benchmark designed to study thinking traces and used to support claims of learned reasoning and planning. Crucially, iGSM exposes the exact quantities and dependencies that a correct solution should use, allowing generated traces to be checked programmatically step by step and enabling us to test whether correct answers are reliably accompanied by valid traces.
We first evaluate models trained exclusively on valid, minimal traces. Answer correctness and trace validity nearly coincide in distribution but decouple out of distribution: on the hardest instances, 31.6 % 31.6\% of correct answers have invalid traces, over half of which pass all syntactic and arithmetic checks but fail semantic dependency checks. We then intervene on trace supervision. Non-minimal training traces induce non-minimal outputs, while re-asking the same problem with a different query reveals computations inherited from the original query, weakening minimality as evidence of selective planning. Shuffling tokens in 10 % 10\% of training trace sentences preserves near-clean accuracy even out of distribution despite no trace passing verification. Swapped training traces likewise retain high in-distribution accuracy.
We discuss the implications of these findings for chain-of-thought monitoring and interpretation in the context of AI safety.
blocks.zh:
思维链痕被广泛解读为模型如何达到答案的记录,告知调试,代理审计,以及推理的主张. 测试这种解释很困难,因为自然语言的思维痕迹很少是机械可核查的. 我们在iGSM中重温它,这是一个综合的年级数学基准,旨在研究思维痕迹,并用来支持对学到的推理和规划的主张. 关键是,iGSM揭示了正确解决方案应使用的确切数量和依赖性,使生成的痕迹能够按程序逐步检查,并使我们能够测试正确答案是否可靠地伴有有效的痕迹.
我们首先评价那些只受过有效、微小痕迹训练的模型。 答案正确性和微量有效性在分布中几乎吻合,但与分布脱节:在最困难的情况下,31.6%的正确答案有无效的痕迹,其中一半以上通过所有综合和算术检查,但没有通过语义依赖性检查。 然后我们介入追踪监控 非微量训练痕迹诱导非微量输出,同时通过不同的查询重新询问同样的问题,揭示了从原始查询中继承的计算,弱化了最小度作为选择性规划的证据. 尽管没有微量通过核实,但10%的训练跟踪句子中的摇动符号仍然保持接近干净的准确性。 抽查的训练痕迹同样保持了高度的分发准确性。
我们讨论了这些结论对在AI安全范围内进行思维链监测和解释的影响。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting ( Wei et al., 2022 ) became popular as a technique for eliciting step-by-step solutions from large language models (LLMs), and substantially improved performance on a range of reasoning tasks. Subsequent work showed that it can be elicited via simple Zero-shot-CoT ( Kojima et al., 2022 ) prompting: “Let’s think step by step”. Soon CoT was incorporated into training as well. STaR ( Zelikman et al., 2022 ) iteratively generates reasoning traces, retains those that lead to the correct final answer, and fine-tunes the model on these successful traces. These results established that model-generated intermediate reasoning could serve both as additional computation at inference time and as a source of training signal.
blocks.zh: 思维链(CoT)促动(Wei等人,2022年)作为一种从大语言模型(LLMs)中引出分步解决的方法而流行起来,并在一系列推理任务上大大提高了性能. 随后的研究表明,可以通过简单的零射-CoT(Kojima等人,2022年)诱导: " 让我们一步一步思考 " 。 很快,CoT也被纳入培训。 STaR(Zelikman等人,2022年)迭代生成推理痕迹,保留导致正确最终答案的推理痕迹,并在这些成功痕迹上微调模型. 这些结果确定,模型产生的中间推理既可作为推论时间的额外计算,又可作为培训信号的来源。

blocks.en: Modern reasoning models extend this idea to a much larger scale through reinforcement-learning (RL)-based post-training. Models generate extended CoT trajectories, often referred to as ‘thinking traces’ or ‘reasoning traces’, and are rewarded when those trajectories lead to successful outcomes ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Kimi Team et al., 2025 ) . In prominent published training recipes, this reward is primarily outcome based , rather than step-level process rewards. DeepSeek-R1-Zero trains with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , using rule-based rewards for answer correctness and output format without directly considering the content of the reasoning traces ( Guo et al., 2025 ) . Kimi K1.5 likewise evaluates generated reasoning traces largely by whether they lead to a correct final answer ( Kimi Team et al., 2025 ) . Such training therefore directly incentivizes intermediate thinking traces that help produce correct answers, but that does not enforce that the emitted trace is itself a valid derivation of that answer. Process-supervision approaches do attempt to close this gap by assigning feedback to intermediate reasoning steps ( Lightman et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) , but they remain unused in these recipes.
blocks.zh: 现代推理模型通过基于强化学习(RL)的后培训,将这一想法扩展到了更大的范围. 模型产生扩展的CoT轨迹,通常称为 " 思考痕迹 " 或 " 合理痕迹 " ,当这些轨迹导致成功结果时,模型会得到奖励(Guo等人,2025年;Kimi Team等人,2025年)。 在已公布的著名培训方法中,这种奖励主要是基于结果的,而不是步骤一级的过程奖励。 DeepSeek-R1-Zero列车采用集团相对政策优化(GRPO)(Shao et al., 2024),使用规则奖励的答案正确性和输出格式,而没有直接考虑推理痕迹的内容(Guo et al., 2025). Kimi K1.5同样主要通过是否得出正确的最后答案来评价产生的推理痕迹(Kimi Team等人,2025年)。 因此,这种培训直接刺激了中间思维的痕迹,有助于得出正确的答案,但这并不强制说所释放的痕迹本身就是该答案的合理来源。 过程-监督方法的确试图通过给中间推理步骤分配反馈来弥补这一差距(Lightman等人,2024年;Wang等人,2024年),但这些方法在这些配方中仍然未被使用.

blocks.en: At inference time, these models produce natural-language thinking traces that often resemble a coherent sequence of arguments, deductions, plans, and revisions, making it tempting to read them as an account of what the model is doing and why. This becomes especially consequential when reasoning models are embedded in agents : models instructed to adopt particular roles or personas, use tools and take actions in an external environment. In multi-agent settings, many such agents may interact through complex and partially autonomous processes to achieve a given goal, with limited human supervision ( Li et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024 ) . There is also a tendency to conduct post-hoc analysis of the agents’ thinking traces, with the intention of understanding how these interactions unfolded; see e.g. ( Greenblatt et al., 2026 ; Yao et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 在推论时间,这些模型产生了自然语言思维痕迹,这些痕迹往往类似于前后连贯的争论,推理,计划和修改的序列,使得人们很诱人地将这些模型解读为模型正在做什么和为什么. 当推理模型嵌入到代理物中时,这种情况就变得特别严重:被指示采用特定角色或人物,使用工具并在外部环境中采取行动的模型. 在多剂环境下,许多此类制剂可能通过复杂和部分自主的过程进行互动,以实现既定目标,人类监督有限(Li等人,2023年;Wu等人,2024年;Chen等人,2024年)。 还有一个趋势是,对毒剂的思维痕迹进行事后分析,目的是了解这些相互作用是如何展开的;例如,见。 (格林布拉特等人,2026年;姚等人,2026年).

blocks.en: With growing emphasis on AI safety and oversight, thinking traces have become a key interface for monitoring and interpreting model behavior. Researchers use them to assess explanation faithfulness ( Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lanham et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) , detect undesirable strategies such as reward hacking ( Baker et al., 2025 ) , and interpret complex multi-agent behavior ( Greenblatt et al., 2026 ; Yao et al., 2026 ) . A recent METR investigation, for example, analyzed the raw thinking traces of a large group of interacting agents and reported coordination, recruitment of other agents into risky experiments, and an agent’s trace explicitly contemplating sacrificing its own success for the benefit of the collective ( Greenblatt et al., 2026 ) . Popular coverage has framed such coordination as a form of “collective intelligence” ( Lyons, 2026 ; Wong, 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 随着对AI安全和监督的日益强调,思维痕迹已经成为监测和解释模型行为的关键界面. 研究人员利用它们来评估解释的忠诚性(Turpin等人,2023年;Lanham等人,2023年;Chen等人,2025年),发现奖励黑客等不良策略(Baker等人,2025年),并解释复杂的多代理行为(Greenblatt等人,2026年;姚等人,2026年). 例如,最近METR公司的一项调查分析了一大批互动代理商的原始思维痕迹和报告的协调工作、招募其他代理商从事风险实验,以及一名代理商明确考虑为了集体的利益牺牲自己的成功(Greenblatt等人,2026年)。 大众报道将这种协调定为一种“集体情报”(里昂,2026年;黄,2026年)。

blocks.en: The above monitoring, interpretation and analysis all rely, explicitly or implicitly, on an important assumption: the emitted thinking trace is faithful , or at least reliably correlated, to how the model arrived at its final answer. However, the fact that a thinking trace is useful to the model for producing a correct answer does not, by itself, establish this. It does not even establish that the emitted trace is a valid derivation of the final answer. Understanding when, how and to what extent thinking traces can be reliably interpreted as records of a model’s reasoning is the central motivation of our work .
blocks.zh: 上述监测、解释和分析都明确或含蓄地依据一个重要假设:释放出的思维痕迹是忠实的,或至少可靠地与模型如何达成最终答案相关。 然而,思维跟踪对产生正确答案的模式有用这一事实本身并不能证明这一点。 它甚至没有确定所释放的痕迹是最后答案的有效来源。 了解思维痕迹何时、如何和在多大程度上可以可靠地解释为模型推理的记录,是我们工作的核心动机。

blocks.en:
Natural-language thinking traces cannot be checked mechanically, so their
validity is rarely tested directly.
We therefore study iGSM ( Ye et al., 2025a ) , a synthetic
grade-school mathematics benchmark, in which the quantities and dependencies underlying each problem are known and model generated traces can be checked programmatically to identify the causes behind why a trace is invalid.
This lets us separate two questions that are often conflated: Was the final answer correct? and Was the thinking trace a
valid derivation of that answer?

这让我们分开两个经常被拼凑的问题: 最后的答案正确吗? 心思是追踪的,

blocks.en:
Prior work interprets the out-of-distribution generalization, minimal
solutions, and hidden-state probes of models trained on iGSM as evidence of
learned reasoning and planning ( Ye et al., 2025a ) .
We ask what an external observer can justifiably infer about the model’s capabilities and computation from the thinking traces alone.
We therefore ask a precise and directly measurable question: When a model produces the correct final answer, does the emitted thinking trace constitute a valid derivation of that answer? If a correct answer is frequently accompanied by an invalid trace, then properties of that trace cannot be used straightforwardly as evidence for the model’s underlying reasoning process.

我们问,一个外部观察者可以合理地从思维的痕迹中推断出模型的能力和计算。
因此,我们提出一个精确和直接可以衡量的问题: 当一个模型产生正确的最终答案时,释放出的思维痕迹是否构成该答案的有效衍生? 如果正确的答案往往伴随着无效的追踪,那么这种追踪的特性就不能直接用作模型基本推理过程的证据。

blocks.en:
We carry out a series of experiments to investigate the above and other related questions on the interpretability of thinking traces. We use the setting of Ye et al. : training GPT-2 ( Radford et al., 2019 ) size models trained on iGSM problem instances.
Our first experiment evaluates models trained only on standard valid, minimal traces, which we call the clean model. Answer correctness and trace validity nearly coincide in distribution, but diverge as reasoning depth moves out of distribution. On the hardest problems, 31.6 % 31.6\% of correct answers are accompanied by invalid traces. Thus, even under the unusually favorable conditions of synthetic data, a fixed trace grammar, clean supervision, and a formally checkable task, a correct answer does not reliably certify the validity of the trace. Further, these failures need not be obvious from a surface inspection: more than half of these invalid traces pass all syntactic and arithmetic checks, and only fail semantic checks based on the problem’s dependencies.
blocks.zh:
我们进行了一系列实验,以调查上述问题和其他有关思维痕迹的解释性问题。 我们使用Ye等人的设置:训练GPT-2(拉德福德等人,2019年)大小模型,训练iGSM问题实例.
我们的首次实验评价了只经过标准有效,最小痕迹训练的模型,我们称之为清洁模型. 答案正确性和痕量有效性在分布上几乎吻合,但在推理深度向分布外移动时却有所不同. 在最困难的问题上,31.6%的正确答案伴有无效的痕迹。 因此,即使在异乎寻常的有利条件下,即合成数据、固定跟踪语法、清洁监督以及正式可核查的任务,正确的答案也无法可靠地证明跟踪的有效性。 此外,这些失败不必从表面检查中看出来:这些无效的痕迹有一半以上通过所有综合和算术检查,只有基于问题依赖性的语义检查失败。

blocks.en:
The analysis of the clean model also identifies a concern for interpreting thinking traces under distribution shift . As problem difficulty increases beyond what was seen during training, the gap between answer correctness and trace validity grows wider.
These failures arise despite training on valid thinking traces, and without any incentives to conceal behavior.
This could have implications for AI safety, trace monitoring and interpretation: thinking trace reliability on familiar tasks could deteriorate when the input distribution shifts.
blocks.zh:
对清洁模型的分析也查明了在分配转移中解释思维痕迹的关切。 随着问题难度超过培训期间所看到的程度,答案正确性和痕量有效性之间的差距越来越大。
尽管在有效思维痕迹方面进行了培训,而且没有任何隐蔽行为的动机,但还是出现了这些失败。
这可能对人工智能安全、跟踪监测和解释产生影响:在输入分布转移时,思考熟悉任务的跟踪可靠性可能会恶化。

blocks.en:
Next, we intervene on the trace supervision and on the query. Training on valid but non-minimal traces substantially changes the minimality of generated
solutions, while re-asking the same problem about a different quantity reveals
computations inherited from the original query. These results show that
minimality alone is insufficient evidence that the model independently selected
exactly the computations required by the current question.

blocks.en:
Finally we consider stronger interventions that destroy trace semantics more directly.
Models trained on traces swapped between unrelated problems still answer 82 % 82\% of in-distribution problems correctly, despite never emitting a valid trace. Next, models trained on traces where 10 % 10\% tokens of the prefix sentences are randomly shuffled, nearly preserve clean-traces model accuracy, even out of distribution, again with no generated trace passing verification. Larger shuffling progressively harms generalization.
The above results along with the results on non-minimal traces establish two points. First, a trace can help the model while being far from a valid derivation. Second, features of the trace that look like reasoning, such as minimality, and coherence can be inherited from the training data rather than worked out by the model.
blocks.zh:
最后,我们考虑采取更有力的干预措施,更直接地破坏微量语义。
在不相关问题上互换痕迹的模型仍然能正确回答82%的分布问题,尽管从未释放出有效的痕迹。 其次,在前缀句子的10% 的 10QQ 符号随机洗牌的痕迹上训练的模型,几乎保存了干净的跟踪模型的准确性,甚至没有分布,再次没有生成的痕量通过验证. 更大的摇摆逐渐损害一般化.
上述结果和关于非最小痕迹的结果确定了两点。 首先,追踪可以帮助模型,同时远离有效的推导. 第二,类似推理的追踪特征,如最小性,以及一致性,可以从培训数据中继承,而不是由模型确定.

blocks.en:
Our conclusions are deliberately narrower than “chain-of-thought does not matter.”
An invalid emitted trace does not show that no useful reasoning occurred internally, and our experiments do not measure whether the trace is a faithful record of the computation that produced the answer. Rather, they show that answer correctness, trace validity, and other properties such as minimality can come apart, and that their
relationship deteriorates under distribution shift. This is important when the thinking traces are used as evidence about how a model reasons or as a signal for interpretation and monitoring. Recent work has proposed monitoring reasoning traces for reward hacking and other undesirable
behavior ( Baker et al., 2025 ; Korbak et al., 2025 ) , while other
studies find that important causal influences may go unmentioned in the
generated reasoning ( Chen et al., 2025 ) . A setting such as iGSM, in which
trace validity can be checked exactly, therefore provides a controlled
test environment of a condition that any stronger claim about the meaning of
thinking traces must satisfy.

blocks.en:
Grade-school mathematics, and GSM8K in
particular ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) , is a foundational benchmark for
reasoning in language models, and step-by-step solutions there play a dual
role: they improve answer accuracy and are read as visible evidence of the
reasoning that produced the answer. Ye et al. (2025a) introduced iGSM,
a synthetic counterpart whose every problem carries its full dependency
structure, and interpreted out-of-distribution generalization, minimal
solutions and hidden-state probes of models trained on it as evidence that
the models learn to reason and plan. Later work used iGSM to study error
correction ( Ye et al., 2025b ) and extended the graph-based construction
to larger problems ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) .

Several findings caution against reading traces as reliable accounts of a
model’s reasoning. Plausible CoT explanations can omit factors that causally
influence the answer ( Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lanham et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) .
More recently, models have produced correct answers while emitting
semantically invalid traces in maze planning ( Valmeekam et al., 2026 ) and
in question answering ( Bhambri et al., 2026 ) . Those studies used
benchmarks built for the purpose. iGSM, in contrast, is an existing
benchmark designed and used in an influential prior effort that arrived at
largely positive conclusions about trace semantics, which lets us test those
conclusions on their own evidence. In chain-of-thought monitoring for AI
safety ( Baker et al., 2025 ; Korbak et al., 2025 ) , an outside monitor reads the trace and looks for problems, which is the role our checker plays. This works only if the trace tells the monitor enough about how the model got to its answer. Our results show how often the trace is invalid even when the answer is right. Appendix A extends

blocks.en: 3 Background
blocks.zh: 3 背景情况

blocks.en:
GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) is a widely used benchmark for evaluating the mathematical reasoning abilities of language models. It
contains 8.5 8.5 K grade-school mathematical word problems with natural-language solutions.
Although the arithmetic involved is elementary, solving these problems often
requires identifying relevant quantities, understanding their dependencies, and
performing a sequence of computations. Ye et al. (2025a) introduced iGSM , a
GSM8K-like synthetic dataset, to study how language models learn such multi-step reasoning. Synthetic generation is useful for several reasons. First, the
training and evaluation distributions are completely controlled, substantially
reducing concerns about data contamination and memorization of existing
problems. Second, the generator can produce a very large and diverse collection
of problems; Ye et al. estimate more than 90 90 trillion distinct solution
templates even after ignoring numerical values, surface forms, variable names,
sentence ordering, and irrelevant parameters. Third, properties such as
reasoning length can be explicitly controlled, allowing models to be trained on
shorter problems and evaluated on longer ones. Finally, the generator retains
the complete symbolic computation underlying every problem, and hence can
produce a valid reference trace and automatically
check generated reasoning traces.

Because every quantity has a name and a definition, a generated trace can be
checked against the problem step by step. The evaluator parses the trace, then verifies that every name used was
defined earlier, that each definition uses exactly the inputs the
dependency graph prescribes, that the arithmetic is right modulo 23, and
that the trace ends by defining the queried parameter. A trace passing all
four checks is valid ; the answer the model states is compared with
the true value separately. Writing 21 × 16 = 15 21\times 16=15 would fail the
arithmetic check. Defining Manatee’s Organs as A + w A+w instead of Q + w Q+w would fail the dependency check even though A A and Q Q share the value
21, because the check compares the parameters a step reads with those
prescribed, not their values. The check does not consider the operation that combines two quantities; this can result in a valid trace with a wrong answer
(Example 9 in Appendix D ).

Table 3 distinguishes syntactic from semantic failures. A syntactic failure is detectable from the trace alone, because the trace does not parse, uses a symbol it never defined, or gets an equation wrong. A semantic failure passes those checks and shows only when the trace is compared with the problem, because a step reads a quantity the dependency graph does not prescribe or defines a name the problem does not contain. The latter account for 95.0 % 95.0\% , 78.1 % 78.1\% , and 51.2 % 51.2\% of invalid traces accompanying correct answers at 𝗈𝗉 = 15 , 20 , 23 \mathsf{op}=15,20,23 . Hence, even with exclusively valid training traces, distribution shift leads to outputs that can remain syntactically and arithmetically plausible while no longer constituting valid derivations of the problem. Since clean traces nevertheless substantially improve out-of-distribution accuracy (Tables 1 and 2 ), computational usefulness and trace validity are
distinct properties. This makes distribution shift an important consideration
for trace-based interpretation and monitoring.

blocks.en:
Our results separate two properties that are easy to conflate: whether a
thinking trace is useful computation for producing an answer, and
whether the emitted trace is itself a correct derivation of that answer.
Clean traces clearly help with the former. Models trained on clean iGSM traces
generalize far better to problems with increased reasoning depth than models trained on swapped or
heavily shuffled traces (Tables 1 and 2 ). The swapped and shuffled interventions carry different claims.
The shuffled models show that a trace can be useful while never valid. With 30 % 30\% of sentences shuffled the model scores 75 % 75\% at 𝗈𝗉 = 15 \mathsf{op}=15 against 25 % 25\% with no trace at all. The swapped models show that a trace
can be pure ritual. The model answers 82 % 82\% of in-distribution problems
while every trace it writes belongs to another problem. Yet the clean model’s advantage does not preserve trace
validity. The share of correct answers with an invalid trace rises from 0.5 % 0.5\% at 𝗈𝗉 = 15 \mathsf{op}=15 to 31.6 % 31.6\% at 𝗈𝗉 = 23 \mathsf{op}=23 (Figure 3 ), and at 𝗈𝗉 = 23 \mathsf{op}=23 half of those traces
pass every syntactic and arithmetic check
(Table 3 ). Thus, under a reasoning-length
distribution shift, traces can retain the form of a plausible derivation
while increasingly losing their problem-specific semantics.

This failure mode is relevant to trace interpretation and CoT-based
oversight ( Korbak et al., 2025 ; Guan et al., 2026 ; Shah & Dragan, 2026 ) .
Note that our experiments do not measure causal faithfulness or the accuracy of a safety
monitor, and we do not dispute that CoT monitoring can remain useful even when traces are imperfect. Our point is that an observable prerequisite for semantic interpretation—that the trace is valid for the problem it purports to solve—can degrade under distribution shift, even in an ideal setting: clean supervision, no adversary, and no incentive to conceal anything. Hence, correct outputs with highly plausible-looking traces alone are insufficient evidence that the semantics of the trace are trustworthy. Therefore, assuming that any reliability established on familiar tasks will transfer over to harder or unfamiliar ones, is unjustified in our view.

blocks.en:
Taken together, these experiments go beyond establishing answer–trace
decoupling. Within iGSM, a benchmark designed to study and
furnish evidence for claims of learned reasoning and planning ( Ye et al., 2025a ; Ye et al., 2025b ) , they test which properties of the visible trace are tied to successful computation and which can instead arise from supervision and problem construction.
The results suggest that trace semantics matter for generalization, but useful intermediate computation need not coincide token-for-token with a correct, externally interpretable derivation.
The broader methodological lesson is that generated traces are observations of model behavior , not direct measurements of the reasoning process inside the model. Their validity, minimality, coherence, and
problem-specific meaning can be shaped by supervision and problem construction,
and their relationship to the final answer can change under distribution shift.
Inferring a reasoning mechanism from these properties therefore requires
counterfactual tests, not observation alone.

结果表明,微量语义对一般化很重要,但有用的中间计算不必与一个正确、外部可解释的推论相吻合。
更广泛的方法教训是,生成的痕迹是对模型行为的观察,而不是对模型内部推理过程的直接测量. 其有效性、最低限度性、一致性和

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We have shown that in iGSM, where thinking traces are mechanically
verifiable, correct answers can come with invalid traces even when the model is trained exclusively on valid,
minimal traces. The fraction of correct answers accompanied by invalid traces
rises from below 1 % 1\% in distribution to 31.6 % 31.6\% on the hardest problems,
and over half of those invalid traces pass all syntactic and arithmetic checks.
Minimality is strongly shaped by supervision and query placement, so minimal
traces alone do not establish planning; meanwhile, training on swapped or
shuffled traces can preserve substantial answer accuracy despite producing no
valid traces. Our models are small and synthetic, so direct extrapolation to
frontier systems is unwarranted, but the simplicity and exact verifiability of
iGSM make these failures harder to dismiss, not easier. Whether thinking traces
of frontier models remain reliable under distribution shift must be tested
directly, not just inferred from correct answers and plausible-looking traces.

blocks.en:
Extra tokens between a question and its answer can help even when they carry no meaning. Goyal et al. (2024) add a learnable pause token and find gains when it is used in both pretraining and finetuning, though the number of pause tokens has to be tuned per task. Pfau et al. (2024) replace chain of thought with repeated filler tokens and show that on a synthetic parallelizable task like 3SUM there is a minimal loss of performance over parallelizable CoT. However, filler training does not seem to recover the behaviour of standard, serial CoT.
With prompting, demonstrations whose reasoning steps are wrong keep most of the benefit of correct ones, as long as the steps stay relevant and in a sensible order ( Wang et al., 2023 ) .
Truncating or corrupting a model’s own trace often leaves its answer unchanged, though how often depends on the task ( Lanham et al., 2023 ) . Kambhampati et al. (2026) argue from results like these that intermediate tokens should not be read as thoughts. Our swapped traces fall between filler and real chain of thought. They are well formed and look like solutions, but they belong to a different problem.
blocks.zh:
问题和答案之间的额外标志即使没有意义,也会有所帮助。 Goyal等人(2024年)在预训和微调中使用时,会添加一个可学习的暂停符号,并找到收益,尽管每个任务必须调制暂停符号的数量. 普法尔等. (2024)用重复的填充符取代思维链,并显示在3SUM这样的合成并行任务上,比起可并行的CoT,性能损失最小. 然而,填充者培训似乎无法恢复标准、系列CoT的行为。
只要这些步骤仍然相关, 并保持合理秩序,
断断续续或腐蚀模型本身的踪迹往往不会改变答案,尽管多少时候取决于任务(Lanham等人,2023年). Kambhampati等人(2026年)从这些结果中认为,中间符号不应被理解为思想。 我们互换的痕迹 介于填充物和真正的思维链之间 它们形成得很好,看起来像是解决办法,但它们属于不同的问题。

blocks.en:
Most of the work above judges traces by their effect on the answer, since natural-language traces cannot be reliably checked by a program, requiring human judgment or a learned verifier. Uesato et al. (2022) had humans label errors in GSM8K solutions and found that outcome supervision gives about the same final-answer error as process supervision, but more correct answers reached through wrong steps. Lightman et al. (2024) make a similar point on MATH, where grading by the final answer alone counts a solution as correct when the answer is right and the steps are wrong. Bhambri et al. (2026) obtain the same separation without human labels. Working in question answering with a rule-based problem decomposition, they build fine-tuning sets in which each problem is paired with either a verifiably correct or a verifiably incorrect CoT trace while the final solution is always correct. Correct traces lead to correct solutions on only 28 % 28\% of test problems, and incorrect traces do not necessarily degrade solution accuracy, so trace correctness and answer correctness are not reliably coupled. They also study end-user interpretability, where the traces that produce the best models are not the ones readers find most interpretable. Valmeekam et al. (2026) demonstrated a striking separation between the semantics of reasoning tokens and the correctness of the final output for maze solving.
In that setting, the intended reasoning trace corresponds to the execution of a formal search algorithm and can therefore be checked mechanically. They show that models could produce correct plans despite invalid traces. Moreover, training on completely unrelated traces still retains much of the benefit of training on valid traces.
Our study follows their setup, but in grade-school math, where the traces are derivations rather than search logs, and where prior work has argued that models trained on this data reason through their traces ( Ye et al., 2025a ) .
blocks.zh:
以上作品大多通过对答案的影响来判断,因为自然语言的痕迹无法被一个程序可靠地检查,需要人类的判断或者一个有学识的核实者. Uesato等人(2022年)在GSM8K解决方案中存在人类标签错误,发现结果监督给出的最终答案错误与过程监督相同,但通过错误步骤得到的答案更正确. Lightman et al. (2024)在MATH上提出了类似的观点,其中仅通过最后的答案进行分级就算作一个在答案正确和步骤错误时的解决方案是正确的. Bhambri等人(2026年)在没有人类标签的情况下获得同样的分离. 在以基于规则的问题分解来回答问题时,它们构建了微调组,每个问题都与可核查的正确性或可核查的不正确的CoT跟踪配对,而最终解决方案总是正确的. 正确的痕迹只导致28%的28QQ测试问题的正确解决方案,不正确的痕迹并不一定会降解溶液的准确性,因此痕量正确性和答案正确性无法可靠地结合. 他们还研究最终用户的解释性,在那里产生最佳模型的痕迹不是读者认为最能解释的. Valmeekam等人(2026年)展示了推理符的语义学与最终输出的正确性对于迷宫解析的显著区别.
在此设定中,意图推理追踪对应执行正式的搜索算法,因此可以机械地检查. 它们表明,尽管有无效的痕迹,模型还是可以产生正确的计划. 此外,完全无关痕迹的培训仍然保留着有效痕迹培训的许多好处。
我们的研究遵循了他们的设定,但是在年级数学中,痕迹是衍生出来的,而不是搜索日志,以前的工作论证过,模型通过自己的痕迹来进行数据方面的训练(Ye等人,2025a)。

blocks.en:
Ye et al. (2025a) train GPT-2 models on iGSM problems with up to 15 or 21 operations and find that they stay accurate on problems that need more operations than any seen in training. They take this as evidence that the model learned to reason rather than memorize templates. Their accuracy counts a solution only if every step is valid, so it does not tell us how answer correctness and trace validity relate as the problems get harder. On general pretrained language models, there is a notable loss in performance compared to the previous setup. Finetuning on GSM8K variants with one extra clause does not transfer to variants with two ( Mirzadeh et al., 2025 ) , and accuracy on GSM-Infinite falls off along a sigmoid as the number of operations grows ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) . In the problem of solving mazes, the swapped-trace models of Valmeekam et al. (2026) generalize well, and sometimes best, on out-of-distribution maze types.
In our setting, where difficulty grows with the number of operations, answer accuracy of the swapped-trace model drops sharply relative to models trained on correct traces as the number of operations grows. One explanation is that the out-of-distribution mazes change the structure within a fixed grid, whereas harder iGSM problems require more serial computation because they involve more operations.
This is consistent with the view that trace content becomes more important as the required computation exceeds what can be captured in a single forward pass ( Emmons et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
Ye et al. (2025a)在iGSM问题上对GPT-2型号进行最多15或21次操作的训练,发现它们对于需要比训练中任何一次都多操作的问题保持准确. 他们认为这是模型学会理性而不是记住模板的证据。 只有每个步骤都是有效的,它们的准确性才算一个解决办法,因此它没有告诉我们,随着问题变得更加严重,答案的正确性和痕量有效性如何相关。 在一般的预训语言模型上,与之前的设置相比,性能明显下降. 对带有一个附加条款的GSM8K变体进行精细调整不会转移到带有两个变体的变体(Mirzadeh等人,2025年),随着操作次数的增加,GSM-Infinite上的精度会随着Sigmoid的出现而下降(Zhou等人,2025年). 在解决迷宫的问题中,Valmeekam等人(2026年)的互换追踪模型对流出迷宫类型进行了很好的概括,有时也是最好的.
在我们的设定中,随着操作次数的增加,困难增加,随着操作次数的增加,互换追踪模型的答题精度与训练有素的正确跟踪模型相比急剧下降. 一种解释是,离散的迷宫会改变固定网格内的结构,而更严重的iGSM问题需要更多的串行计算,因为它们涉及更多的操作.
这符合一种观点,即微量内容变得更加重要,因为要求的计算超过了在一次前行通行证中可以捕获的内容(Emmons等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: iGSM ( Ye et al., 2025a ) generates problems from a hierarchy of categories and a random dependency graph, with arithmetic mod 23, so every solution can be checked step by step by a program. GSM-Infinite builds on a similar graph construction, reworks the noisy data generator, drops the modulus, adds division and a reverse mode, and scales the number of operations and the context length for evaluating pretrained models ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) . GSM-Symbolic turns GSM8K test problems into templates and finds large variance across instances, and big drops when an irrelevant clause is added ( Mirzadeh et al., 2025 ) . Both benchmarks score only the final answer. GSM-Symbolic traces are free-form and cannot be checked by a program reliably. GSM-Infinite has the graphs needed to check them, but does not use them for that. Given our results, accuracy curves on these benchmarks may not say much about whether the reasoning behind them is correct.
blocks.zh: iGSM 系统 (Ye et al., 2025a)从分类的等级和随机依赖图产生问题,带有算术的mod 23,因此每个解决方案都可以通过程序一步步检查. GSM-Infinite基于相似的图形构造,重修噪音数据生成器,放下模组,增加分割和反向模式,并缩放操作数量和上下文长度,用于评价预试模型(周等人,2025年). GSM-Symbolic将GSM8K测试问题转化为模板,发现各种情况差异很大,在添加不相关条款时出现大跌(Mirzadeh等人,2025年). 这两项基准只得到最后的答案。 GSM-Symbolic的痕迹是自由形式的,无法由程序可靠地检查. GSM-Infinite有检查它们所需的图表,但并没有为此使用. 鉴于我们的结果,这些基准的准确性曲线可能没有多少说明它们背后的推理是否正确。

blocks.en:
Reading a model’s chain of thought has become a key tool for oversight. Korbak et al. (2025) and Shah & Dragan (2026) argue that this window is valuable but fragile, and that its value rests on the trace having been optimized to be useful for the answer, not to look a particular way. Guan et al. (2026) build evaluations to track monitorability across models and training, and find that most current frontier models are fairly, but not perfectly, monitorable. Other work shows how monitorability can break.
Penalizing bad reasoning in the trace during RL leads to reward hacking with benign-looking traces ( Baker et al., 2025 ) , penalizing specific strings leads to encoded reasoning ( McCarthy et al., 2025 ) , and models finetuned only on documents describing a monitor learn to leave their misbehavior out of the trace ( Haskins et al., 2026 ) .
Some prompted models can also hide a side task from a monitor under enough pressure ( Zolkowski et al., 2025 ) . Emmons et al. (2025) find that models
struggle to evade monitors on tasks that require chain of thought, and Brown-Cohen et al. (2026) bound how much serial computation a transformer can do without writing it down.
Our setting has no adversary, no monitor in the loop and no pressure on the trace to be optimal.
Even so, correct answers often come with invalid traces, more so on harder
problems. The answer accuracy of our swapped-trace models collapses only once problems get large, which is consistent with the necessity view. But a trace being necessary does not make
it correct, so a monitor can read a necessary trace and still see the wrong
derivation.
blocks.zh:
阅读模型的思想链已成为监督的关键工具。 Korbak等人(2025年)和Shah & Dragan (2026年)认为,这一窗口是有价值的但脆弱的,其价值在于已经优化的追踪对答案有用,而不是看一个特定的方式. 关等人. (2026) 建立评价,以跟踪跨模型和培训的可监测性,并发现目前大多数前沿模型是公平但并非完全可监测的。 其他工作显示可监测性如何打破.

blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Pericardium’s Monocytes equals the sum of each Cheetah’s Organs and each Cheetah’s Mitral Valve. The number of each Cheetah’s Mitral Valve equals each Great Victoria Desert’s Cells. The number of each Gobi Desert’s Cheetah equals 11 times as much as each Great Victoria Desert’s Creatures. The number of each Gorilla’s Pericardium equals the sum of each Gobi Desert’s Creatures, each Gobi Desert’s Gorilla and each Gobi Desert’s Cheetah. The number of each Pericardium’s Eosinophils equals the sum of each Gorilla’s Organs, each Gorilla’s Pericardium and each Pericardium’s Monocytes. The number of each Gobi Desert’s Gorilla equals 12. How many Cells does Gobi Desert have? Model trace. Define Great Victoria Desert’s Creatures as a; so a = 0. Define Gobi Desert’s Cheetah as b; so b = 11 * a = 11 * 0 = 0. Define Gobi Desert’s Gorilla as P; so P = 12. Define Gobi Desert’s Creatures as p; so p = b + P = 0 + 12 = 12. Define Gorilla’s Pericardium as o; B = p + P = 12 + 12 = 1; so o = B + b = 1 + 0 = 1. Define Gorilla’s Organs as c; so c = o = 1. Define Great Victoria Desert’s Cells as w; so w = 0. Define Cheetah’s Mitral Valve as m; so m = w = 0. Define Cheetah’s Organs as f; so f = m = 0. Define Pericardium’s Monocytes as r; so r = f + m = 0 + 0 = 0. Define Pericardium’s Eosinophils as K; A = c + o = 1 + 1 = 2; so K = A + r = 2 + 0 = 2. Define Pericardium’s Cells as X; so X = r + K = 0 + 2 = 2. Define Cheetah’s Cells as k; so k = m * X = 0 * 2 = 0. Define Gorilla’s Cells as S; so S = o * X = 1 * 2 = 2. Define Gobi Desert’s Cells as H; M = b * k = 0 * 0 = 0; j = P * S = 12 * 2 = 1; so H = M + j = 0 + 1 = 1. Answer. 1 Checker. Invalid, at the step in bold. Cheetah’s only organ is Mitral Valve, so Cheetah’s Cells should be Cheetah’s Mitral Valve (m) times Mitral Valve’s Cells. The trace instead multiplies m by X, which is Pericardium’s Cells, the total for a different organ. Because m = 0, the product is 0 either way, and the answer is unaffected.
blocks.zh: 问题 每一个Cericardium的单体数目等于每个Cheetah的器官和每个Cheetah的Mitral阀门的总和。 每个Cheetah的Mitral阀门的数目相当于每个大维多利亚沙漠的细胞。 每个戈壁沙漠的Cheetah数量相当于每个大维多利亚沙漠的物种的11倍. 每个戈壁沙漠的大猩猩和每个戈壁沙漠的猎豹的总和。 每个Pericardium的Eosinophils数等于每个Gorilla的器官,每个Gorilla的Pericardium和每个Pericardium的Monocytes的总和. 每个戈壁沙漠的大猩猩的数量等于12。 戈壁沙漠有多少个细胞? 模式追踪。 将大维多利亚沙漠的生物定义为a;所以是=0. 将戈壁沙漠的猎豹定义为b;所以b=11 * a=11 *0 =0. 将戈壁沙漠的大猩猩定义为P;所以P=12. 将戈壁沙漠的生物定义为p;因此p=b + P= 0 + 12 = 12. 将大猩猩的心臟定义为o;B=p + P= 12 + 12 = 1;因此o=B + b= 1 + 0 = 1. 将大猩猩的器官定义为c;因此c=o = 1. 将大维多利亚沙漠的细胞定义为w;所以w= 0. 将Cheetah的Mitral阀门定义为m;因此m=w= 0. 将Cheetah的器官定义为f;因此f=m= 0. 将环心ium的单体定义为r;所以r = f + m = 0+ 0= (单位:千美元) 0,将Pericardium的Eosinophils定义为K;A = c + o = 1 + 1 = 2;所以K = A + r = 2 + 0 = 2. 将Pericardium的细胞定义为 X;所以X = r + K = 0 + 2 = 2. 将Cheetah的细胞定义为 k;所以K = m * X = 0 * 2 = 0. 将Gorilla的细胞定义为 S;所以S = O = 1 * 2 = 2. 将Gobi Desert的细胞定义为 H;M = b * k = 0 = 0 = 0;j = P = S = 12 * 2 = 1;所以H = M + j = 0 + 1 = 1. 回答 1 跳格. 无效, 以粗体表示 。 Cheetah唯一的器官是Mitral Valve,因此Cheetah的细胞应该是Mitral Valve(m)乘以Mitral Valve的细胞. 微量乘以X,即Pericardium的细胞,是另一个器官的总数。 因为m=0,所以产品是0的任意一种,而答案没有受到影响.

blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Arctic Ocean’s Stork equals 3 times as much as the sum of each Tidal Pool’s Creatures and each Owl’s Autonomic Nerves. The number of each Arctic Ocean’s Owl equals 0. The number of each Autonomic Nerves’s Plasma Cells equals 22 more than the sum of each Arctic Ocean’s Creatures and each Arctic Ocean’s Owl. The number of each Autonomic Nerves’s Basophils equals the difference of each Tidal Pool’s Organs and each Tidal Pool’s Creatures. The number of each Stork’s Thalamus equals 7 more than each Owl’s Organs. The number of each Owl’s Autonomic Nerves equals the sum of each Tidal Pool’s Cells and each Arctic Ocean’s Owl. How many Cells does Arctic Ocean have? Model trace. Define Arctic Ocean’s Owl as f; so f = 0. Define Tidal Pool’s Cells as s; so s = 0. Define Owl’s Autonomic Nerves as R; so R = s + f = 0 + 0 = 0. Define Tidal Pool’s Creatures as W; so W = 0. Define Arctic Ocean’s Stork as X; v = W + R = 0 + 0 = 0; so X = 3 * v = 3 * 0 = 0. Define Arctic Ocean’s Creatures as r; so r = f + X = 0 + 0 = 0. Define Autonomic Nerves’s Plasma Cells as O; P = r + f = 0 + 0 = 0; so O = 22 + P = 22 + 0 = 22. Define Tidal Pool’s Organs as J; so J = 0. Define Autonomic Nerves’s Basophils as x; so x = J - W = 0 - 0 = 0. Define Autonomic Nerves’s Cells as A; so A = O + x = 22 + 0 = 22. Define Owl’s Cells as U; so U = R * A = 0 * 22 = 0. Define Stork’s Thalamus as o; so o = 7 + U = 7 + 0 = 7. Define Thalamus’s Cells as k; so k = 0. Define Stork’s Cells as L; so L = o * k = 7 * 0 = 0. Define Arctic Ocean’s Cells as b; q = f * U = 0 * 0 = 0; z = X * L = 0 * 0 = 0; so b = q + z = 0 + 0 = 0. Answer. 0 Checker. Invalid, at the step in bold. The underlined sentence says Stork’s Thalamus is 7 more than Owl’s Organs, but the trace adds 7 to U, which is Owl’s Cells. Both are 0, so every later value, and the answer, is unchanged.
blocks.zh: 问题 每个北冰洋的Stork的数量相当于每个潮池的生物和每个猫头鹰的自动神经器的总和的3倍。 每个北冰洋的猫头鹰数量等于0.。 每个自动纳维斯的等离子细胞数量比每个北冰洋的生物和每个北冰洋的猫头鹰的总和多22个。 每个自动纳维斯的Basophils的数目等于每个潮池的器官和每个潮池的生物的区别。 每个Stork的Tharamus数量比每个猫头鹰的器官多7个。 每个猫头鹰的自动神经细胞的数目等于每个潮池细胞和北冰洋的猫头鹰的总和。 北冰洋有多少个细胞? 模式追踪。 将北冰洋的猫头鹰定义为f;因此f=0. 将潮池的单元格定义为 s; s = 0,将猫头鹰的自动神经器定义为R;因此R=s+f=0+0= 0,将潮池的生物定义为W;因此W=0. 将北冰洋的Stork定义为X;v=W+R=0+0;因此X=3*v=3*=0=0. 将北冰洋的生物定义为r;因此r=f+X=0+0=0. 0,将自动神经器的等离子细胞定义为O;P = r + f = 0 + 0 = 0;故O = 22 + P = 22 + 0 = 22. 将潮池的器官定义为J;故J = 0,将自动化神经细胞定义为x;所以x=J - W=0=0=0. 将自动化神经细胞定义为A;所以A=O+x=22+0=22. 将Owl的细胞定义为U;所以U=R*A=0*22=0. 将Stork的Thalamus定义为o;所以O=7+U=7+0=7. 将Thalamus的细胞定义为k;所以K=0. 将Stork的细胞定义为L;所以L=O*K=7*0=0. 将北冰洋的细胞定义为b;q=f*U=0*0=0;z=X=L=0=0=0;因此b=q+z=0=0+0=0. 回答。 0 检查器。 无效, 以粗体表示 。 下划线的句子写着Stork的Tharamus比Owl的器官多7个, 两者均为0,所以每个后期值,答案不变.

blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Ecology Lab’s Sweat-Resistant Backpack equals each Harbortown University’s Stationery. Define Eastwood University’s Classroom as G; so G = F + z = 0 + 0 = 0. Define Golf Backpack’s Correction Tape as w; so w = G = 0. Define Golf Backpack’s Stationery as m; so m = w = 0. blocks.zh: 问题 每个生态实验室的汗水-呼吸距离背包的数量相当于每个港城大学的文具。 每个Eastwood大学植物学实验室的数量是每个生态学实验室的背包的7倍。 Golf Backpack的校正磁带数量相当于Eastwood大学的教室。 每个Eastwood大学的生态实验室的数量相当于每个生态实验室的Sweat-Resistant Backpack的2倍. 每个生态实验室的高尔夫背包的数量相当于每个港镇大学文具和每个生态实验室的柔软背包的8倍。 每个Sweat-Resistant Backpack的Binder Clip的数量等于每个港城大学的Backpack. 东林大学有多少文具馆?. 模式追踪。 将港城大学的文具定义为u;所以u=0. 将生态实验室的Sweat-Resistant Backpack定义为g;所以g=u= 0,将生态实验室的高尔夫背包定义为R;W = u - g = 0 - 0 = 0;因此R = 8 * W = 8 * 0 = 0. 将生态实验室的背包定义为o;所以O = R + g = 0 + 0 = 0. 0,将伊斯特伍德大学的植物学实验室定义为z;所以z=7*o=7*0=0. 将伊斯特伍德大学的生态学实验室定义为F;所以F=2*g=2*0=. 将东木大学的教室定义为G;因此G=F+z=0+0= 0. 将Golf Backpack的校正磁带定义为w;因此w=G= 0. 将高尔夫背包的文具定义为m;因此m=w= 0. 将植物学实验室的文具定义为L;因此L= 0,将生态实验室的文具定义为A;T=R *U=0;K=g*米=0;因此A=T+K+0;Eastwood大学的文具定义为c;v=F=A=0;B=z=L=0;因此C=0=0;因此Eastwood大学的文具定义为c;v=F=F=A=0;B=z=L=0;n=0=0;n=0=0;n=0=0;n=0=0. 0+0=0. 答. 0 检查器. 无效, 以粗体表示 。 条款 T = R * U 使用从未定义过微量的资本 U;它只定义小写 u,值为 0. 这个问题的每个数量都是0,所以答案没有受到影响.

blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Tidal Pool’s Dragonfly equals each Dragonfly’s Laryngopharynx. The number of each Tidal Pool’s Woodpecker equals 13 times as much as each Dragonfly’s Laryngopharynx. The number of each Arctic Ocean’s Dragonfly equals 3 more than each Tidal Pool’s Organs. The number of each Tidal Pool’s Pigeon equals each Coastal Ecosystem’s Organs. The number of each Woodpecker’s Pleural Cavity equals each Coastal Ecosystem’s Organs. The number of each Arctic Ocean’s Pigeon equals the difference of each Tidal Pool’s Dragonfly and each Dragonfly’s Laryngopharynx. The number of each Dragonfly’s Laryngopharynx equals 17. The number of each Woodpecker’s Oropharynx equals 4 times as much as each Coastal Ecosystem’s Creatures. How many Organs does Arctic Ocean have? Model trace. Define Dragonfly’s Laryngopharynx as a; so a = 17. Define Tidal Pool’s Dragonfly as p; so p = a = 17. Define Coastal Ecosystem’s Organs as b; so b = 0. Define Dragonfly’s Organs as o; so o = a = 17. Define Tidal Pool’s Pigeon as r; so r = b = 0. Define Pigeon’s Organs as B; so B = 0. Define Tidal Pool’s Woodpecker as f; so f = 13 * a = 13 * 17 = 14. Define Tidal Pool’s Organs as x; W = p * o = 17 * 17 = 13; h = r * B = 0 * 0 = 0; q = W + h = 13 + 0 = 13; Y = f * q = 14 * 0 = 0; so x = q + Y = 13 + 0 = 13. Define Arctic Ocean’s Dragonfly as S; so S = 3 + x = 3 + 13 = 16. Define Arctic Ocean’s Pigeon as A; so A = p - a = 17 - 17 = 0. Define Arctic Ocean’s Organs as G; K = S * o = 16 * 17 = 19; J = A * B = 0 * 0 = 0; so G = K + J = 19 + 0 = 19. Answer. 19 Checker. Invalid, at the step in bold. The clause should multiply Tidal Pool’s Woodpecker, f, by Woodpecker’s Organs, which is 0 and which the trace never defines. Instead it writes f * q, naming the partial sum q just computed, whose value is 13, while substituting the 0 it needed. The checker flags the reference to q. Because the intended factor is 0 either way, the product and the answer are unaffected.
blocks.zh: 问题 每个潮池的"龙蝇"数量等于每个"龙蝇"的Laryngopharynx. 每个潮池的啄木鸟数量相当于每个龙蝇的Laryngopharynx的13倍. 北冰洋的龙蝇数量比潮池的每个器官多3只。 每个潮水池的鸽子数量等于每个沿海生态系统的器官。 每只啄木鸟的花瓶数量相当于每个沿海生态系统的器官。 每个北冰洋的Pigeon的数量等于每个潮池的龙蝇和每个龙蝇的Laryngopharynx的区别. 每只龙蝇的Laryngopharynx的编号等于17. 每个啄木鸟的Oropharynx的数量是每个沿海生态系统的生物的四倍。 北冰洋有多少器官? 模式追踪。 将"龙蝇"的Laryngopharynx定义为a;所以a=17. 将潮池的飞龙定义为p;所以p=a=17. 将沿海生态系统的器官定义为b;所以b= 0. 将龙蝇的器官定义为o;所以o=a=17. 将潮池的 Pig定义为r;所以r=b= 0. 将Pigeon的器官定义为B;因此B= 0,将潮池的啄木鸟定义为f;所以f=13 * a=13 * 17 =14. 将潮池的器官定义为x;W=p*o=17 *17 =13;h=r *B=0 =0 =0;q=W+h=13 +0 =13;Y=F=q =14 =0;所以x=q + Y=13 =0 =13 =0;所以将北冰洋的龙蝇定义为S;所以S=3 +x =3 +13 =16. 将北冰洋的皮格龙定义为A;A=P=a=17 - 17 =0 0. 将北冰洋的器官定义为G;K=S=16 =17 =19;J*B=0 =0 =0 =0 =0;所以G=K+J=19 +0 =19 答复。 无效, 以粗体表示 。 条款应该将潮池的啄木鸟乘以啄木鸟的器官, 相反,它写 f * q, 命名刚计算的 q 部分和 q, 其值为 13, 同时替换它所需要的 0 。 检查者标出参考q. 由于预期因子为0,因此产品和答案不受影响.

blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Historic Industrial District’s Boxed equals each Historic Downtown’s DoorDash. The number of each DoorDash’s Sparkling Water equals each Wine’s Cherry. The number of each Deliveroo’s Wine equals 13 times as much as the sum of each Historic Industrial District’s Supermarket and each Historic Downtown’s DoorDash. The number of each Wine’s Cherry equals 1. The number of each Wine’s Mango equals the sum of each Quarters’s Product, each Quarters’s Deliveroo, each Deliveroo’s Product and each Wine’s Cherry. The number of each Sparkling Water’s Lemon equals 13. The number of each Deliveroo’s Almond Milk equals 11 more than the difference of each DoorDash’s Wine and each Almond Milk’s Ingredient. The number of each Historic Downtown’s DoorDash equals 16 times as much as the difference of each DoorDash’s Sparkling Water and each Wine’s Cherry. The number of each DoorDash’s Wine equals 14 times as much as the difference of each Historic Industrial District’s Boxed and each DoorDash’s Sparkling Water. The number of each Quarters’s Deliveroo equals 7 more than the difference of each Almond Milk’s Ingredient and each Historic Downtown’s DoorDash. The number of each Historic Downtown’s Boxed equals the sum of each Historic Downtown’s DoorDash, each DoorDash’s Ingredient, each Wine’s Cherry and each Quarters’s Ingredient. How many Mango does Wine have? Model trace. Define Wine’s Cherry as c; so c = 1. Define DoorDash’s Sparkling Water as w; so w = c = 1. Define Historic Downtown’s DoorDash as A; B = w - c = 1 - 1 = 0; so A = 16 * B = 16 * 0 = 0. Define Historic Industrial District’s Boxed as K; so K = A = 0. Define DoorDash’s Wine as b; J = K - w = 0 - 1 = 22; so b = 14 * J = 14 * 22 = 9. Define Almond Milk’s Ingredient as M; so M = 0. Define Deliveroo’s Almond Milk as G; f = b - M = 9 - 0 = 9; so G = 11 + f = 11 + 9 = 20. Define Historic Downtown’s Deliveroo as P; z = M - A = 0 - 0 = 0; so P = 7 * z = 7 * 0 = 0. Define Quarters’s Deliveroo as r; h = M - A = 0 - 0 = 0; so r = 7 + h = 7 + 0 = 7. Define Historic Industrial District’s Supermarket as E; so E = K = 0. Define Deliveroo’s Wine as a; O = E + A = 0 + 0 = 0; so a = 13 * O = 13 * 0 = 0. Define Deliveroo’s Product as X; so X = G + a = 20 + 0 = 20. Define Quarters’s Product as R; so R = r * X = 7 * 20 = 2. Define Wine’s Mango as k; S = R + r = 2 + 7 = 9; q = S + X = 9 + 20 = 6; so k = q + c = 6 + 1 = 7. Answer. 7 Checker. Invalid, at the step in bold. No sentence of the problem mentions Historic Downtown’s Deliveroo. blocks.en: Problem. The number of each Amboseli National Park’s Zebra Paddock equals 7. The number of each Serengeti National Park’s Cheetah Run equals 9 times as much as the difference of each Serengeti National Park’s Zebra Paddock and each Amboseli National Park’s Animal. The number of each Bat Cave’s Squirrel equals 9 times as much as the sum of each Zebra Paddock’s Squirrel and each Zebra Paddock’s Animal. The number of each Amboseli National Park’s Bat Cave equals 13 more than the sum of each Zebra Paddock’s Animal and each Otter Pool’s Kangaroo. The number of each Zebra Paddock’s Squirrel equals 7 more than the difference of each Amboseli National Park’s Otter Pool and each Otter Pool’s Kangaroo. The number of each Serengeti National Park’s Zebra Paddock equals 5 more than each Amboseli National Park’s Animal. The number of each Amboseli National Park’s Otter Pool equals each Otter Pool’s Kangaroo. The number of each Otter Pool’s Kangaroo equals 22. How many Cheetah Run does Serengeti National Park have? Model trace. Define Otter Pool’s Kangaroo as a; so a = 22. Define Amboseli National Park’s Otter Pool as b; so b = a = 22. Define Zebra Paddock’s Squirrel as P; z = b - a = 22 - 22 = 0; so P = 7 + z = 7 + 0 = 7. Define Zebra Paddock’s Animal as p; so p = P = 7. Define Amboseli National Park’s Bat Cave as G; Y = p + a = 7 + 22 = 6; so G = 13 + Y = 13 + 6 = 19. Define Bat Cave’s Squirrel as S; h = P + p = 7 + 7 = 14; so S = 9 * h = 9 * 14 = 11. Define Bat Cave’s Animal as k; so k = S = 11. Define Amboseli National Park’s Zebra Paddock as r; so r = 7. Define Amboseli National Park’s Animal as g; q = G * p = 19 * 7 = 18; B = b * k = 22 * 11 = 12; c = q + B = 18 + 12 = 7; s = r * k = 7 * 11 = 8; so g = c + s = 7 + 8 = 15. Define Serengeti National Park’s Zebra Paddock as J; so J = 5 + g = 5 + 15 = 20. Define Serengeti National Park’s Cheetah Run as K; f = J - g = 20 - 15 = 5; so K = 9 * f = 9 * 5 = 22. Answer. 22 Checker. Invalid, at the step in bold. Amboseli National Park’s Animal should be the sum over its three exhibits of the exhibit count times that exhibit’s Animal, 19 × 11 + 7 × 7 + 22 × 22 19\times 11+7\times 7+22\times 22 , which is 6. The trace pairs every exhibit with another exhibit’s Animal and never reads Otter Pool’s Animal, so the dependency check fails and the step gives 15. The wrong value flows on through the two underlined sentences. Serengeti National Park’s Zebra Paddock is 5 more than it, and Cheetah Run is 9 times the difference of the two. That difference is 5 whatever the value, so the answer is 22 either way.
